hypotheses.name: spontaneous pneumomediastinum (e.g., due to alveolar rupture from coughing, Valsalva, or asthma exacerbation)
hypotheses.basis: Mediastinal air without pneumothorax or trauma history is classic for spontaneous pneumomediastinum; subcutaneous extension supports this. Requires clinical correlation for symptoms (e.g., retrosternal pain, dyspnea, Hamman’s crunch).

hypotheses.name: esophageal perforation (Boerhaave syndrome)
hypotheses.basis: Pneumomediastinum + subcutaneous emphysema can occur, but typically more severe clinical picture and often associated with recent vomiting/retching; absence of pleural fluid or mediastinal widening makes this less likely without further data.
